name: trueforge-coder
description: Editor-native coding agent for VS Code whose agent loop runs on TrueForge (github.com/truefoundry/trueforge).

commands.title: TrueForge Coder: Undo Last Agent Changes
TrueForge Coder: Register Editor Tools in TrueForge
TrueForge Coder: Set Up NVIDIA Models (enter API key)
TrueForge Coder: Choose Model / Fallback Chain

trueforgeCoder.baseUrl.description: URL of the local TrueForge server (npx @truefoundry/trueforge).

trueforgeCoder.mcpPort.description: Port of the editor MCP server this extension hosts for TrueForge.

trueforgeCoder.mcpServerName.description: Name of the connector registered in TrueForge for the editor MCP server.

trueforgeCoder.models.description: Ordered model chain as TrueForge model names (provider/model). If the first fails, the next is used automatically.

trueforgeCoder.contextBudgetTokens.description: Token budget for automatically retrieved code context.

trueforgeCoder.rollbackOnCancel.description: Pressing Stop reverts every file the cancelled run already changed, so a cancelled multi-file change is all-or-nothing. Turn off to keep hunks you already approved.

trueforgeCoder.retries.description: Retries (with exponential backoff) on the same model before falling back to the next one.

trueforgeCoder.compactionTriggerTokens.description: TrueForge compacts the agent context once it passes this many input tokens (0 = TrueForge default). Kept low because free-tier models slow down and hit rate limits on long contexts.

trueforgeCoder.autoApproveCommands.description: Run the commands the agent asks for (for example pytest) without showing the confirmation dialog. Off by default. Edits to files are never auto-approved: every hunk is still reviewed. You can also click "Allow all commands this session" in the dialog.

trueforgeCoder.commandPreamble.description: Prefix for commands the agent runs (after you approve them), for example ". .venv/bin/activate &&" so pytest and flask come from your virtualenv.
